articles.title: Kimi Antonelli seizes F1 US GP pole and chance to seal first world title
articles.summary: Antonelli has 102-point lead over George Russell. Needs to be 125 points in front after Sunday’s race. Kimi Antonelli claimed pole position for the US Grand Prix with a hugely impressive lap for Mercedes at the Circuit of the Americas.
body: Isack Hadjar did well to secure third for Red Bull, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in fourth and fifth for Ferrari, and Antonelli’s Mercedes teammate George Russell in sixth.

Antonelli’s first pole since the Belgian GP in July could not have been better timed as he attempts to take his first title. The Italian has a 102-point lead over Russell and needs to be 125 points in front after this race. To take the title he must win on Sunday and have Russell finish outside the top eight, with Hamilton outside the top four. The win certainly looks to be a strong prospect but he still needs his rivals to stumble on Sunday.
He can only do his best and knows that even should the title not be secured here, on this form it will surely be done and dusted by the next round in Mexico.

“We got pole, so we’ll try to win tomorrow,” Antonelli said. “Max has been very quick and did an incredible job in qualifying so it’s not going to be easy. Hopefully we’ll be leading into turn one and we’ll try to set the pace, even though it’s going to be very tight. Very happy with qualifying today, Q3 was very tough with the wind, gusty, unpredictable but happy to stick it on pole.”

articles.title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga
articles.summary: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli. Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt. Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples.
body: Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a ‌late consolation through Simone Lontani.

Third-placed Roma ‌trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, so will be pleased with a point in Naples as they preserved ‌their 15-game unbeaten league run that dates back to April. Frank Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gave Napoli the lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage.

At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matías Soulé and Leonardo Balerdi drew Roma level. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining.

articles.title: 'Not realistic' - Can Wolff's assessment of Antonelli's title chance be trusted?
articles.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes it is "not realistic" for Kimi Antonelli to win the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix, despite the Italian starting on pole position.
body: Antonelli was not expected to claim top spot in qualifying but produced a superb lap in Q3 to beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen and take his first pole position since July's Belgian Grand Prix.
Should Antonelli win Sunday's race in Austin with Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower and George Russell ninth or lower, he will seal the title with five rounds remaining.
Hamilton will start fifth and Russell sixth when the lights go out at the Circuit of the Americas at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.
However, Wolff has warned Mercedes will not have the pace to win as they did not have the pace in Friday practice's long runs.

articles.title: Nashville SC seal first MLS Supporters’ Shield with 2-0 win over CF Montreal
articles.summary: Surridge and Mukhtar fire Nashville to 2-0 victory. Nashville extend unbeaten streak to seven matches. Montreal teenager Keita impresses on MLS debut. Nashville SC scored twice in the second half to claim the Supporters’ Shield as the top team in MLS with a 2-0 win at CF Montreal on Saturday.
body: The win allowed Nashville (21-3-7, 70 points) to stretch their unbeaten streak to seven games (5-0-2).
Montreal (6-18-7, 25 points) have just one win in their past 11 games (1-8-2) and have been officially eliminated from playoff contention.

Sam Surridge buried his own rebound to give Nashville a 1-0 lead in the 52nd minute. Montreal goalkeeper Samsy Keita, the 17-year-old homegrown player making his MLS debut, denied Surridge’s header from the right side of the goal area off a cross from Reed Baker-Whiting. The rebound went right to Surridge, who easily put it into the far side for his team-leading 18th goal of the season.

Hany Mukhtar made it 2-0 in the 76th minute. He intercepted defender Brayan Vera’s clearing attempt outside the box, was first to it as it rolled inside the box and then hit a shot that deflected off Keita and into the net from the top right corner of the goal area.

articles.title: Alonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to Spurs
articles.summary: Forward sent off after 80 minutes for second yellow card. ‘We need to have maturity to deal with difficult moments’ Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during Chelsea’s shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, who claimed their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018 thanks to an…
body: Spurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. The playmaker could have been sent off earlier – his first booking came during a clash with Mateus Fernandes – and Alonso agreed that this could be an important lesson for the 24-year-old.

“Absolutely,” Chelsea’s manager said. “I haven’t seen them [back] on TV but as far as I have been told probably he [the referee] got it right. We need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments. When you have conceded for 1-0, still probably it was 15-20 minutes to go. I need to check the action to talk with Cole but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Alonso said there are no wider concerns with Palmer’s character, even though Chelsea’s No 10 could have been sent off against Everton last weekend too. “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a concern,” Alonso said. “It is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature, for everyone.”

articles.title: Antonelli stands on brink of history in Austin
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli can become the youngest F1 world champion on Sunday, but far from feeling the pressure he says he is enjoying himself more than usual.
body: It certainly looked like it on Saturday at the Circuit of the Americas as he took a surprise pole position by 0.179 seconds from Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
Antonelli will become world champion on Sunday if he wins the race while his Mercedes team-mate George Russell is lower than eighth and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton below fourth.

Antonelli had not been on pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July after Mercedes' early season dominance came under challenge from first McLaren and then Red Bull. And his delight was clear as he whooped over the team radio on his slowing down lap.
He came into the weekend insisting he was going to try to apply the "same mindset as I had all year - one race at a time".

Antonelli whooped with delight as he took his first pole position since the Belgian Grand Prix in July and said: "It feels good to be back."

Hamilton is already below that position having qualified fifth, while Russell will start sixth ahead of the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris.

articles.title: 'Dream come true!' - Britain's Palmowski becomes 2026 F1 Academy champion
articles.summary: Britain's Alisha Palmowski became the 2026 F1 Academy champion with three races to spare after building an unassailable lead in Austin.
body: Palmowski followed up victory in Friday's Opening Race at the Circuit of the Americas with second in the Reverse Grid Race behind Alba Larsen to take a 70-point lead over her closest championship challenger, Emma Felbermayr, with only a maximum if 67 points remaining.
The Red Bull-backed has dominated this season by winning five of the 11 races so far with six pole positions to become the second Briton after Abbi Pulling in 2024 to win the F1 Academy title.
Palmowski, 20, is the youngest F1 Academy champion and praised the team and her family, who were in attendance in Austin.
"We did it guys! It's incredible. I don't know what to say. I'm trying not to cry!" she said.

articles.title: Fourth quarter implosion sends WSU to 1-7 in 31-10 loss to No. 21 Boise State
articles.summary: Enterting the final 15 minutes, the one-win Washington State Cougars were tied with the No. 21 Boise State Broncos. Before a critical 4th and 2 for the Bronco offense, most of the WSU team was dancing along to the music blaring over the speakers and the crimson LED lights flashing above.
body: That big play never came for the Cougars. Instead, the Broncos scored just a few plays later, then rattled off two more touchdowns as the Cougars crumbled and watched their once realistic upset bid fade away in a hurry. And with their upset bid, also their slim bowl eligibility hopes.
After dancing and trying to hold the momentum to begin the quarter, it ended with heads hung low as the new scoreboard read 31-10 Boise State.
WSU falls to 1-7 and 0-4 in Pac-12 play, and it marks the quickest WSU has been eliminated from bowl eligibility since 2010.

articles.title: ‘Night and day different’ – why did Ferrari's pace evaporate again?
articles.summary: Ferrari's wait for a first Grand Prix pole position since August 2025 continued in the United States on Saturday as Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top three in a session they had been widely tipped as favourites for.
body: For the first time this season, Ferrari went into qualifying having Ferrari topped all three practice sessions in Austin, on a weekend their car features the team's final significant upgrade of the season.
Leclerc finished second fastest to McLaren's Lando Norris in Q1, but only after the McLaren driver completed a second run to do so, and then was then back at the head of the field in Q2.
But the Scuderia found themselves on the back foot immediately from the start of Q3 with Leclerc holding a provisional fourth and Hamilton sixth after the first runs of the decisive final phase.

Hamilton improved one place to fifth on his final run, but Leclerc stayed where he was, to leave the Ferraris behind the two Red Bull drivers and Mercedes polesitter Kimi Antonelli for the start of Sunday's 56-lap race. Had Leclerc matched his benchmark time from Q2 he would have qualified second.

articles.title: Lionel Messi magic missing as Inter Miami win streak snapped by New York Red Bulls defeat
articles.summary: Inter Miami saw their impressive three-match winning streak come to an end on Saturday night following a disappointing 2-0 defeat against the New York Red Bulls. Despite the introduction of Lionel Messi in the second half, the Herons were unable to overturn an early deficit at the Red Bull Arena.
body: The evening got off to a disastrous start for the visitors in Harrison, New Jersey, when a defensive lapse handed the hosts an early advantage. Just seven minutes into the contest, former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder Casemiro inadvertently diverted the ball into his own net while attempting to deal with a dangerous cross from Cade Cowell. The Brazilian veteran’s failed clearance set the tone for a frustrating outing for Cristian “Kily” González’s side.

Despite holding 62.5% of the possession, Inter Miami struggled to turn it into chances, while New York created the better openings with 18 shot attempts. The loss marked a significant setback for the club, who had been in excellent domestic form prior to their trip to the East Coast.

The result was a bitter pill to swallow for González, who watched his side control large spells of the game without the necessary cutting edge. Miami managed only two shots on target, highlighting a rare lack of precision in the final third.

articles.title: Simply unbelievable! Neymar sent off under the 'Vini Jr law'
articles.summary: Neymar's Saturday night (24th) borders on the unbelievable. After halftime in Santos' 1–0 loss to Bahia at Vila Belmiro, the star No. 10 CONTINUED taunting Rodrigo Nestor before play resumed at the stadium known as the Alçapão.
body: After repeatedly directing comments at the Bahia midfielder, Neymar covered his mouth while arguing with Nestor.
The former São Paulo player then reported the gesture to the referee, who consulted VAR and showed Neymar a red card under the "Vini Jr. Rule."
In effect since the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the rule instructs referees to send off anyone who covers their mouth while arguing with an opponent.
It was introduced after the Brazil and Real Madrid forward suffered racist abuse from Argentina's Gianluca Prestianni during a Champions League match against Benfica.
